from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Method of Exhaustion (Limits)", [
            "Approximate a curve with straight segments.", 
            "More segments make a better approximation.", 
            "As segments shrink, we find the limit."
        ])
        
        # Setup Circle (Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg)

        circle = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg")
        self.place_in_area(circle, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        circle.set_color(WHITE)

        # Initial polygon (triangle)
        def get_polygon(n):
            return RegularPolygon(n=n, radius=1.0, color="#FFFF00")

        polygon = get_polygon(3)
        self.place_in_area(polygon, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.add(polygon)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(circle), FadeIn(polygon))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        for n in range(4, 13):
            new_polygon = get_polygon(n)
            self.place_in_area(new_polygon, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.95)

        self.play(polygon.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(circle.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Zoom in to see a curve's slope.",
            "A tiny section looks like a straight line.",
            "This slope is the derivative at that point.",
            "The derivative tracks rate of change.",
            "It captures motion at a single instant."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Derivative: Seeing the Slope", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        microscope = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/microscope.svg", color=WHITE)
        speedometer = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg", color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(microscope, "A6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.add(microscope)
        
        # Curve Setup
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.1 * x**3 - 0.5 * x + 1, x_range=[-3, 3], color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'C4', 'E6', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        point_marker = Dot(curve.point_from_proportion(0.5), color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(point_marker, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        tangent_line = Line(start=[-1, 0, 0], end=[1, 0, 0], color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(tangent_line, 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(curve), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.play(FadeIn(point_marker))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(curve.animate.scale(2, about_point=point_marker.get_center()), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, "B6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(tangent_line), FadeIn(speedometer))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#ADFF2F")
        self.play(FadeOut(curve), FadeOut(tangent_line), FadeOut(point_marker), FadeOut(microscope), FadeOut(speedometer))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Integrals sum up tiny slices.",
            "Adding infinite slices reveals total area.",
            "It acts as the derivative's opposite.",
            "Think of it as accumulating change.",
            "This bridges tiny parts to the whole."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Integral: Accumulating the Whole", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        ruler = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg")
        graph = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/graph.svg")
        
        # Setup visual
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[0, 1, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.1 * x**3 - 0.2 * x**2 + 0.5, color=BLUE)
        
        # Group for integration visual
        integral_visual = VGroup(axes, curve)
        self.place_in_area(integral_visual, "B3", "E5", scale_factor=0.75)
        
        def get_bars(n):
            bars = VGroup()
            x_vals = np.linspace(-2, 2, n+1)
            f = lambda x: 0.1 * x**3 - 0.2 * x**2 + 0.5
            for i in range(n):
                # Riemann rectangles in Manim CE expect a graph object and x_range
                bar = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(curve, 
                                                x_range=[x_vals[i], x_vals[i+1]], dx=x_vals[i+1]-x_vals[i], color="#FFA500")
                bars.add(bar)
            return bars

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        self.place_at_grid(ruler, "A6", scale_factor=0.5)
        bars_4 = get_bars(4)
        self.play(FadeIn(integral_visual), Create(bars_4), FadeIn(ruler))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.place_at_grid(graph, "F6", scale_factor=0.5)
        bars_20 = get_bars(20)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(bars_4, bars_20), FadeIn(graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Derivative and integral are inverse operations.",
            "They connect splitting and building processes.",
            "Together they reveal the framework of change."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem: The Bridge", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects for animations
        derivative_sym = MathTex(r"\\frac{d}{dx}", color="#00FF00")
        integral_sym = MathTex(r"\\int", color="#00FF00")
        
        # Load bridge asset
        bridge = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg")
        bridge.set_color("#FF4500")

        # Layout formula elements
        self.place_at_grid(derivative_sym, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(integral_sym, 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_in_area(bridge, 'B3', 'B4', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        formula_group = VGroup(derivative_sym, bridge, integral_sym)
        self.place_in_area(formula_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(derivative_sym), Write(integral_sym))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(bridge))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.wait(1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Essence of Calculus: From Motion to Infinitesimal
outline.target_audience: High school students or curious beginners

sections.title: The Paradox of Instantaneous Motion
sections.content: Introduce the fundamental problem: How can we measure speed at a single, static point in time? Use the concept of 'Average vs. Instantaneous' velocity to motivate the need for calculus.
sections.example: A cheetah chasing a gazelle: If the cheetah's speed is changing constantly, the speedometer shows a different number every millisecond.

sections.title: The Method of Exhaustion (Limits)
sections.content: Explain the concept of a 'Limit'. Visualize a curve being approximated by shorter and shorter straight line segments. As the segments become infinitely small, the approximation converges to the curve itself.
sections.example: An animation of a polygon inside a circle; as the number of sides increases, the polygon's perimeter and area 'melt' into the shape of the circle.

sections.title: The Derivative: Seeing the Slope
sections.content: Define the derivative as the 'rate of change' at a single point (the slope of the tangent line). Visually demonstrate the 'zoom-in' effect where a complex curve looks like a straight line at an microscopic level.
sections.example: A mountain climber's path: The derivative represents the exact steepness of the terrain under their feet at any specific second.

sections.title: The Integral: Accumulating the Whole
sections.content: Define the integral as the reverse of the derivative—summing up an infinite number of tiny slices to find a total. Connect this to finding the area under a curve.
sections.example: A robotic arm painting a curved wall: The integral calculates the total amount of paint used by summing up millions of tiny, thin vertical strips of paint.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Bridge
sections.content: Conclude by showing how the derivative (splitting apart) and the integral (putting together) are inverse operations, linking the two seemingly different concepts into one powerful framework.
sections.example: A digital music player: The sound wave is stored as a collection of instantaneous points (derivative-like), and the player 'integrates' them to reconstruct the continuous melody you hear.
